query: Why do I need everything to feel certain?
why_in_two_sentences: Psychology Today gives the academic construct (intolerance of uncertainty, by a leading worry researcher) and PsychCentral gives a five-causes list for controlling behavior. Ours explains the mechanism more usefully (certainty as a fixed need, a learned rule attached to it, and control as the vehicle), and covers the OCD, autism, and ADHD differentials plus the calm-feels-worse paradox in 34 FAQs. (The #6 organic result, a Guardian piece, fetched as 1000 characters behind a consent wall, and the next result failed to fetch; PsychCentral at #9 was judged instead.)
what_we_do_that_they_dont: Splits the fixed need from the learned rule and the vehicle, which turns a pathology label into something adjustable
Explains why things going well triggers anxiety and why calm stretches feel worse than busy ones
Shows the relational cost concretely (the recurring weekend fight, the fury at a ten-minute-late text)
34 verbatim FAQs including OCD, autism, ADHD differentials and whether a certainty need can exist without a difficult childhood

above_the_fold.ours: H1 is the query, the short answer gives the need-rule-vehicle split in four sentences, then recognition sentences; the mechanism arrives before any scrolling.
above_the_fold.theirs: Psychology Today opens with a key-points box defining intolerance of uncertainty and its links to pathological worry; precise and credible, but it reads as a diagnosis of a worrier, not an answer to someone who calls themselves organized.

questions_they_answer_that_we_dont: Can a personality disorder be behind a need to control everything?
trust_signals: Psychology Today shows a named PhD researcher-author writing on his own field; PsychCentral shows medical review by an LMFT; ours names no one and cites nothing.
one_change_with_most_traffic_impact: none - ours covers both competitors' ground with more mechanism and more verbatim long-tail FAQs; the only residual gap is a personality-disorder FAQ.
